symptom: The deprecated request-file CLI had a static runtime import of the executor facade, so even rejected task and unknown modes would evaluate the executor/N2 import graph before the fail-closed gate. The Draft branch now retains only a type import and defers runtime import until after mode denial, request validation and READY task checks. Official CI verified the source-order regression and existing no-request denials. No executor invocation or prior import side effect was observed.
lesson: A terminal CLI mode guard does not prevent eager ESM import evaluation. Keep optional executor and protected-research module graphs behind the already verified fail-closed mode and request gates, using type-only imports for compile-time references.
guardrail: Preserve the type-only executor import and post-READY dynamic import, plus source-order and synthetic no-policy/no-request exit-3 regressions. A green test does not establish live workflow disablement, prove a historical import side effect, activate N2, or authorize any production connection.
